problems.title: The problems we see in practices every week

faq.title: What practice owners and administrators ask us

items.a: It depends on your practice’s model. For fee-for-service we charge a percentage of what is actually collected; for practices under HMO or full-risk contracts, a flat monthly fee. Projects and credentialing are quoted by scope. We send you a written quote once we understand your volume, with no hidden fees.

items.q: How do you access our system?
items.a: Your practice creates an individual user account for each member of our team in your EHR (eClinicalWorks, athenahealth, AdvancedMD, Tebra or another), with two-factor authentication and only the permissions needed. We never use shared passwords, and you can revoke access at any time.

Before we see any patient information, we sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA). We comply with HIPAA through encryption, two-factor authentication, access control, activity logging and annual training for the whole team. There is no official HIPAA certification: what matters are the controls, and we will show them to you.

The 50-note audit is usually delivered within 5 to 10 business days after we receive access. Ongoing service typically starts 2 to 4 weeks after signing, depending on how quickly access and payer enrollments (for example, electronic payments and remittances) are completed.

items.q: Do you work with Medicare, Medicaid and commercial insurance?
items.a: Yes. We work with Original Medicare, Medicare Advantage plans (HMO and PPO), Florida Medicaid plans and commercial insurers. We adapt to the rules of each payer and each of your practice’s contracts.

items.q: What is the difference between full-service billing and a dedicated coder?
items.a: Full-service billing (RCM) covers the entire revenue cycle: coding, claim submission, payments, denials, A/R and reporting. A dedicated coder is a certified professional assigned to your practice who focuses on documentation quality, risk adjustment coding and quality gaps; it is especially useful for practices under HMO or full-risk contracts. Many practices combine both.

Ongoing services have an initial term agreed in the proposal and then renew month to month, with written notice to terminate so pending accounts can be transitioned in an orderly way. Projects are contracted by scope, with no long-term commitment.

We review 50 recent notes selected with you (different providers and visit types). We assess visit level, procedures, diagnosis specificity, support for risk-adjusting conditions, modifiers and quality gaps. You receive a written report with findings, an estimate of legitimate uncollected revenue, the risks in your documentation and recommendations, plus a meeting to walk through it. There is no obligation to sign up.

items.q: Does the coder tell the physician what to diagnose?
items.a: No. The physician always assesses, diagnoses and documents. The coder prepares information from the chart for the physician to review and, when a note is unclear, sends a neutral query without suggesting an answer. We code only what the physician documents and supports.

items.q: Do you offer service in Spanish?
items.a: Yes. Our team works in Spanish and English, with owners and administrators as well as with your front desk and billing staff.

rcm.title: Full-service billing (RCM)
rcm.short: The entire revenue cycle, from note to deposit: coding, submission, payments, denials, A/R and a monthly report.
rcm.summary: We manage your practice’s entire revenue cycle so your staff can focus on patients. Every note is coded, every claim is reviewed before submission and every balance is followed until it is paid or resolved.
includes: Coding of every note (CPT, ICD-10-CM, HCPCS and modifiers) as documented
Patient and insurance data review before submission
Electronic claim submission and correction of clearinghouse rejections
Payment and remittance posting (ERA/EOB) reconciled to deposits
Denial management and appeals within each payer’s deadlines
A/R follow-up by aging bucket and by payer
Patient statements and answers to patient billing questions
Monthly report with metrics and a review meeting
rcm.ideal: Fee-for-service or mixed practices that want to outsource billing end to end or replace their current vendor.

coder.title: Dedicated coder: risk & quality
coder.short: A certified coder (CPC/CRC) assigned to your practice to prepare visits, review notes and close quality gaps.
coder.summary: A certified coder who knows your physicians, your patients and your contracts. They work before and after the visit so documentation accurately and completely reflects each patient’s complexity and the quality measures already met.
includes: A CPC or CRC certified coder assigned to your practice
Visit preparation: chart summary, chronic conditions still to be assessed this year and open quality gaps
Diagnosis support for the problem list: gathers evidence from the chart (labs, specialists, hospital stays) for the physician to evaluate
Note review before closing: specificity, support for each condition (MEAT) and consistency
Neutral physician queries when documentation is unclear
Quality gap work (Stars/HEDIS) and reporting of quality codes
Monthly report on documentation findings and brief physician education
coder.guardrail: The physician always assesses and documents. The coder never diagnoses, never leads the answer in a query and never codes a condition the note does not support.
coder.ideal: Practices with Medicare Advantage patients under HMO (flat rate or capitation) or full-risk contracts.

projects.title: Projects
projects.short: Backlog note cleanup, coding audits and recovery of old accounts receivable.
projects.summary: Work with a defined scope and delivery date, to solve a specific problem or prepare your practice ahead of a change.
includes: Backlog cleanup: we code and submit the backlog, prioritizing timely filing limits
Coding audits: visit level (E/M), procedures, risk adjustment, pre-bill or retrospective
Old A/R recovery: balance-by-balance review, correction, resubmission and appeal where appropriate
Overpayment identification and support for timely repayment
Final report with findings, actions taken and recommendations
projects.ideal: Practices switching billing vendors or EHRs, carrying a backlog, or preparing for an audit.

credentialing.title: Credentialing
credentialing.short: Enrollment and maintenance of your providers with Medicare, Medicaid, Medicare Advantage plans and commercial payers.
credentialing.summary: A provider who is not properly enrolled does not get paid. We handle enrollments, renewals and expirations so no physician ends up out of network because of pending paperwork.
includes: CAQH ProView profile setup and attestation
Medicare (PECOS) and Florida Medicaid enrollment
Participation applications with Medicare Advantage plans and commercial payers
Electronic payment and remittance enrollment (EFT/ERA)
Recredentialing and tracking of license, DEA and malpractice expirations
Status log for every application, shared with your practice
credentialing.ideal: Practices adding new providers, opening a new location or cleaning up lapsed enrollments.

compliancePage.title: We protect your patients and your practice
compliancePage.lead: Accurate, complete coding is only valuable if it is also defensible. These are the controls we work with.

sections.title: We comply with HIPAA
sections.text: There is no official HIPAA certification. What exists are concrete controls, and these are ours:
items: A Business Associate Agreement (BAA) signed with every client before any access
Encryption of data in transit and at rest
Two-factor authentication on every system
Access control: individual accounts, minimum necessary access and immediate revocation at offboarding
Annual HIPAA training for the entire team
Incident response and notification procedures in line with the Breach Notification Rule
Periodic security risk assessments

sections.title: Compliance program based on OIG guidance
sections.text: We follow the elements of an effective compliance program described by the Office of Inspector General (OIG) of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services:
items: Written coding and billing policies and procedures
A designated compliance officer
Ongoing team training
Open channels to report questions or concerns, without retaliation
Internal auditing and monitoring
Consistently enforced disciplinary standards
Prompt response and corrective action, including repayment of identified overpayments
Screening of staff against the OIG exclusion list (LEIE)

sections.title: Coding based only on documentation
sections.text: We code what the physician assessed and documented, nothing more and nothing less.
items: The physician always assesses, diagnoses and documents; the coder never diagnoses
Every risk-adjusting condition must be supported in the note (monitored, evaluated, assessed or treated)
Neutral, non-leading physician queries
When a code is not supported we flag it, even if it lowers reimbursement
If we find an overpayment, we help you report and return it on time

sections.title: U.S.-based team
sections.text: Every team member with access to your patients’ information works from the United States.
items: No offshore subcontracting for work involving patient information
Background checks before hiring
Confidentiality agreements signed by every team member

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains how {legalName} (“{company}”, “we”) handles the personal information it receives through this website. It does not apply to patient information we process on behalf of our clients, which is governed by our service agreements and HIPAA Business Associate Agreements (BAAs).

sections.title: 1. Information we collect
paragraphs: Information you provide in the contact form: name, title, practice name, city, phone, email, number of providers, contract type, service of interest and any message you write.
Aggregated, anonymous usage data, such as pages visited, country and device type, collected through an analytics tool that does not use cookies or identify individuals.
This website is not designed to receive protected health information (PHI). Please do not include it. If we receive it by mistake, we will delete it.

sections.title: 2. How we use it
paragraphs: To respond to your request, prepare a quote or arrange the note audit; to improve the website; and to meet legal obligations. We do not sell or rent your personal information and we do not use it for third-party advertising.

sections.title: 3. Who we share it with
paragraphs: With vendors that provide technical services needed to run the website, such as web hosting and email delivery, under confidentiality obligations. We may also share it when required by law.

sections.title: 4. Cookies and analytics
paragraphs: This website does not use advertising cookies or third-party tracking pixels. The analytics we use do not set cookies and work with aggregated data.

sections.title: 5. Retention
paragraphs: We keep form data as long as needed to handle your request and maintain the business relationship, and thereafter for the period required by applicable legal obligations.

sections.title: 6. Security
paragraphs: We apply reasonable technical and organizational measures to protect your information, such as encryption in transit and restricted access. No system is completely secure, so we cannot guarantee absolute security.

sections.title: 7. Your choices
paragraphs: You can ask us to access, correct or delete your information, or to stop receiving communications, by writing to {email}.

sections.title: 8. Children
paragraphs: This website is intended for healthcare professionals and businesses. We do not knowingly collect information from children under 13.

sections.title: 9. Changes and contact
paragraphs: We may update this policy. We will post the current version on this page with its update date. If you have questions, write to {email} or call {phone}.
